answerlines: Spain [or Kingdom of Spain or España or Reino de España]

clues.text: The last track of the album Return to Forever is named for this country and was composed by Chick Corea (kuh-REE-uh).
Martha Graham choreographed a solo dance created in response to a war in this country titled for a style called “deep song.”
A song called “Will o' the Wisp” appears on side one of an album named for this country, whose tracks “The Pan Piper” and “Saeta” (sai-AY-tuh) were written by Gil Evans.
A former natural history museum in this country holds paintings such as The Garden of Earthly Delights.
One composer from this country wrote a ballet that contains the Fire Dance and portrays Caramelo (“CAR-uh-MELL-oh”), called Love, The Magician.
In this country, an eighteen-spired cathedral combining Gothic and Art Nouveau styles has been under construction since 1882, and was designed by Antoni Gaud´ı.
An opera based on a legend from this country features the title character being dragged to hell by a statue of the Commendatore.
Name this country home to Manuel de Falla and Isaac Albeniz, the latter of which composed a work titled “Iberia.”
Name this country, where Figaro prepares for his wedding after serving as the title “Barber of Seville.”
Name this European country that was written about in Albeniz's (“AL-ben-eez’s”) Iberia and whose toreadors are characters in Carmen.

answerlines: Spain [or Kingdom of Spain or España or Reino de España]

clues.text: One opera set in this country depicts three masked guests stopping an assault at a party that is proposed during the aria “Till They Are Tipsy.”
In this country, a roof arched like the back of a dragon and a turret representing St. George’s lance appear on top of the “House of Bones.”
This nation is also home to a museum with a giant puppy sculpted by Jeff Koons from flowers and a cathedral with a Passion Facade designed by Josep Maria Subirachs.
Josep Jujol collaborated with an architect from this country to design a house nicknamed “The Stone Quarry.”
A colorful salamander is in this country’s Park Güell (“gwail”), which was designed by the same architect who created one building’s Nativity and Passion façades.

Teo Macero (TAY-oh mah-SAY-roh) produced a Miles Davis album titled for Sketches of this country, which includes the second movement of native composer Joaquín Rodrigo's (wah-KEEN rah-DREE-gohz)Concierto de Aranjuez(kahns-YAIR-toh day-rahn-WEZ).
An opera based on a legend from this country features the title character being dragged to hell by a statue of the Commendatore.
Dances from this country include the bolero, jota, and seguidilla.
Name this European country of Manuel de Falla, who wrote the ballet El amor brujo.
Name this home of Santiago Calatrava, Antoni Gaudi, and the Guggenheim Bilbao.

answerlines: Spain [or Kingdom of Spain; or España; or Reino de España]
Spain [or Espana; accept equivalent answers like “the Spanish Republic,” etc.]

clues.text: Alexander Gorsky's 1900 revival of a ballet set in this country added a variation in which a fan is repeatedly snapped open and shut by Kitri.

Moderator Note: Read lowercase numerals (i.e. i) in the chords as “minor” (i.e. “minor one“) and capital as "major" This country names a chord progression whose first half is “i, V, i, VII, III, VII, i, V,” known as its “follies.”
The gigue ("zheeg") was often paired with a triple-meter dance from this country that usually comprised the third movement of four-movement suites.
A style of still-life set in the kitchen called bodegón evolved in this country.

Themes from this country also inspired that composer for the fourth movement of his piano suite Miroirs. Édouard Lalo composed a five-movement piece for violin and orchestra titled after this country.
A large ear grows from a tree in a painting set on a farm in this country titled The Tilled Field.
Home to the composer of the ballet The Three-Cornered Hat and the keyboard sonatas of Antonio Soler, another composer from this country, Isaac Albeniz, wrote a piano suite named Iberia.
Instruments created in this country include the vihuela and a namesake five-stringed guitar.
Name this European country with a strong classical guitar tradition.
Name this country home to the Sagrada Familía and the Guggenheim Bilbao.
